Counterpoint- Even if it would give him a broader appeal, it might affect his audience to be more indifferent to his works as a whole.

Let's say hypothetically that currently Milo has 100 fans, of which 50 look forward to everything he posts while the other 50 are pretty indifferent, if he didn't gloat or didn't make his personality as out there potentially he might have 110 fans, but only 20 who look forward to everything he posts, this would be a net loss of fans as the more 'casual' observers are generally a kind of temporary market, you can't expect to hold onto any of them for extended periods of time, as they generally don't view what you have to offer them to be significantly worth the time/effort to keep up to date on and read, so as time goes on they'll probably either find someone whom they enjoy more and thus see less value in what Milo specifically offers, or they might get really busy at work for a couple of weeks and thus their time/effort go up in value which results in them falling behind on Milo's content, and once they aren't keeping up to date it would become a bit more difficult to get back into it, and since in the first place it didn't offer a 'significant' return on investment and they're aware of this they probably would just stop following him entirely.

One has to balance not only how 'big' of an appeal they have, but how 'dedicated' of an appeal they have, as without a strong 'dedicated' following then you're essentially risking your livelihood everyday that no one who offers more of what your audience wants will walk in and steal your audience. More 'casual' audience is a short-term gain that will come and go, and it's good to appeal to them at the very least to spread the word about your stuff more (to try to grab more 'dedicated' followers), but if you can't retain a strong 'dedicated' audience then you're probably going to end up as click-bait, because that's ultimately the biggest short-term 'eyeball' grab currently known for this kind of media.
